Definition: properly, abrupt, i.e. a precipice; by implication, the front; used only adverbially (with prepositional prefix) opposite
BiblicalUsage: Mul means in front of, over against, before — hearken now unto my voice, Jethro says to Moses, I will give thee counsel, and God be with thee; Balak sends for Balaam who dwells over against the river; and Moses speaks to all Israel on this side Jordan, in the wilderness, over against the Red Sea.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the little word is the Bible's way of saying where things stand: before God, before the river, before the people — and the standing is the story.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
